title: Golden Cuts beyond Plato
description:
Slice a four-dimensional cube, the tesseract, straight across its longest diagonal and every slice is a tetrahedron with its corners cut off. At two golden heights the cuts are exactly the golden cuts of #88, one either side of the classical truncated tetrahedron at half height. The golden dodecahedra appear the same way in the 120-cell, so four of the five golden pairs of the regular solids are slices of regular four-dimensional solids. Beyond the regular solids golden cuts are rare: a solid with two kinds of face never has one; two solids come close, with every face golden or regular; two rhombic solids have their own golden pair; and the four star polyhedra of Kepler and Poinsot have two each.

In #88 we showed that each Platonic solid has exactly two golden cuts, the Greater and Lesser Golden Cut solids, and that the icosahedral and octahedral pairs are sections of the 120-cell and the 24-cell. DICTO proposed carrying the golden cuts beyond the Platonic solids. Our main theorem is four-dimensional: the sections of the tesseract perpendicular to a long diagonal, between its two middle layers of corners, are exactly the tetrahedra cut at x = (1 − h)/(2 − h), so that the Greater Golden Cut Tetrahedron, the Archimedean truncated tetrahedron and the Lesser Golden Cut Tetrahedron are the sections at heights 1/φ², 1/2 and 1/φ; the golden tetrahedra are also sections of the 120-cell, and the Greater and Lesser Golden Cut Dodecahedra are its cell-first sections at 1/φ² and 1/φ of the way between two layers of corners. Hence the golden pairs of the dodecahedron, icosahedron, tetrahedron and octahedron are all sections of regular four-dimensional solids; the golden cubes were not found in the directions searched. Beyond Plato: the twelve golden cut depths of the regular triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon, octagon and decagon are all different, so no Archimedean solid has a cut making every face golden; only the icosidodecahedron and the snub dodecahedron have cuts making every face golden or regular, two each, at 1/(φ√5) and 1/3 (for the icosidodecahedron, Zefiro's 2011 regular-decagon and regular-hexagon stages, here read as golden); among the Catalan solids only the rhombic dodecahedron and the rhombic triacontahedron have golden cuts, exactly two each, in closed form; and each Kepler–Poinsot star polyhedron has two. All results are exact in the number fields of the solids, except where stated.

The idea of carrying the golden cuts of #88 beyond the Platonic solids, the choice of this research, the golden cuts themselves and the names of the families are DICTO's. Computation, proofs, exact checks and drafting with Claude (Anthropic).
